target.title: Simplify cost labels and clarify estimate provenance
target.body:
## Summary

Simplify cost navigation labels and move the general cost explanation from the menu into Cost settings.

- Rename provider cost buttons and sections to the consistent label `Cost`
- Move the general reported-versus-estimated explanation to the bottom of Cost settings
- Keep one short Codex-specific note beside its displayed values:
  `Estimated from token usage · not a subscription bill`
- Remove repeated explanations and obsolete localized labels from menu and chart views
- Keep the CLI label explicit because CLI output has no surrounding UI context

## Why

The previous menu mixed navigation labels with explanations such as “API-equivalent estimate” and “Token-based cost estimate.” This caused three problems:

1. The labels were long and frequently truncated.
2. The same Cost destination had different names depending on the provider.
3. A single estimate-focused label was not accurate for every provider: some costs are provider-reported, while others are calculated from token usage.

A button should clearly describe where it leads, so all provider buttons now use the concise label `Cost`.

Moving the general explanation out of the menu also lets cost entries with submenus use a standard native menu row instead of a custom multi-line SwiftUI card. This restores consistent menu sizing, highlighting, and interaction behavior.

The general explanation applies to the Cost feature as a whole, not to one menu item. It now appears in Cost settings, where users can see that values may be provider-reported or estimated from token usage at public API prices, and that estimates are not subscription charges.

Codex keeps a short explanation directly under its dashboard details because its prominent dollar values are token-derived and could otherwise be mistaken for an actual bill. This provides the necessary context without repeating the full explanation throughout the menu.

The CLI retains `Codex token-based cost` because terminal output must explain itself without relying on the menu or settings UI.

## Result

The menu is shorter and more consistent, while the distinction between reported costs, token-derived estimates, and subscription billing remains available where users need it.

## Validation

- Focused cost, menu, settings, CLI, and localization tests: 134 passed
- `make test`: all 718 selections passed
- `make check`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`

target.title: Fix StepFun login web ID
target.body:
## Summary

- derive the StepFun login web ID from the anonymous token before building the Cookie header
- add a regression assertion for the complete password-login Cookie header

## Root cause

The login request interpolated `self.webID`, which is a function reference after `webID(forToken:)` was introduced. Swift emitted a warning and the resulting Cookie header could contain a function debug description instead of the required web ID.

## Impact

Password-based StepFun fallback login now sends a valid `Oasis-Webid` value and the production build no longer emits the function-interpolation warning.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter StepFunTokenRefreshTests` — 8 tests passed
- `swift build -c release` — passed without the StepFun warning
- `make check` — passed

target.title: Serialize flaky Claude CLI platform-gating cases
target.body:
## Summary

- serialize only the two parameterized Claude CLI platform-gating cases
- preserve the per-mode assertion that logged-out `.auto` and `.cli` runs invoke only `auth status --json`
- keep the containment test-only; no production concurrency behavior changes

Fixes #2309.

This flake surfaced in #2292's unrelated Linux x64 shard. Both parameterized cases started together and failed the same invocation assertion even though each already uses UUID-scoped binary and log paths. The deeper shared runtime boundary is not proven, so this PR takes the narrowest safe containment.

- `make check` — passed; 0 SwiftFormat changes and 0 SwiftLint violations across 1,572 files
- `make test` — passed all 716 selections in 60/60 groups, no retries or timeouts

Linux x64 CI is the authoritative regression gate for the originally observed flake.

## Exact-head Linux proof

- Linux arm64 passed on the same commit: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659074330/job/88118445750

Both jobs retained the full Linux test step and CLI smoke test. The remaining macOS jobs are queued and unchanged by this `TestsLinux`-only diff.

target.title: Fix black PNG exports from usage share cards
target.body:
## Summary

- render usage share cards with SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` instead of an offscreen `NSHostingView.cacheDisplay`
- preserve the exact 1200×630 PNG contract
- strengthen the renderer regression test so a valid-but-uniform black PNG fails

Fixes #2286.
Part of #2291.

## Production evidence

The installed 0.44.0 (build 106) app returned a structurally valid 1200×630 PNG from **Copy Image**, but every pixel was black:

```text
size=1200x630 colors=1 min=0 max=0 mean=0
```

The final renderer tree (`ddd39620`, unchanged by tree-identical CI retry head `d4e836fb`) rendered the same synthetic payload through `ShareStatsRenderer.pngData(for:)` as visible, non-uniform output:

```text
size=1200x630 colors=1032 min=4112 max=65535 mean=21126.8
```

![Synthetic usage share card rendered from the unchanged renderer tree](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/ddd39620/docs/screenshots/share-stats-renderer-after.png)

The screenshot uses synthetic fixture data only. It was freshly generated from the final renderer path after the maintainer's no-Metal revision.

## Verification

- `swift test --filter ShareStatsTests` — 12 tests passed on the unchanged renderer tree
- `file` / `sips` — RGBA PNG, exactly 1200×630
- ImageMagick pixel inspection — 1,032 colors; non-uniform visible output
- `make check` — passed, including SwiftFormat and SwiftLint
- `make test` — 715/715 selections passed across 60/60 groups, with zero retries and zero timeouts

## CI evidence

`d4e836fb` is an empty, tree-identical retry commit because contributor permissions cannot rerun a failed GitHub job directly.

- exact-head Linux x64 passed the full test and CLI smoke steps: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659631050/job/88119915545
- exact-head Linux arm64 passed: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659631050/job/88119915479
- exact-head Linux musl build passed: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29659631050/job/88119934685
- both macOS shards passed on the identical renderer tree before the retry commit: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29657985495/job/88115675488 and https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/actions/runs/29657985495/job/88115675496
